relevant_D_paragraphs: as in [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Let $D$ be the Levi–Civita derivative of $h$, let $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$, and put $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK$. Define the scalar and magnetic-potential residuals

1. $C_i=0$ and $B_{ij}=0$ persist, so $\pi_i=D_i\varphi$ and $F=dA$.
2. The scalar equation gives $\nabla_a j^a=0$, and the sourced Maxwell evolution together with the two initial Gauss constraints gives $dF=0$ and $d\star_gF=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$.
3. Before Einstein-equation recovery, $\nabla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab})=0$.
4. The metric first-order derivative variables remain derivatives of the metric, and harmonic gauge propagates; hence the reduced Einstein equation is the full Einstein equation.

1.1 Differentiate $C_i$ in $s$ and group the compatibility equation from [L2]: $\partial_sC_i=(\partial_s\pi_i-\partial_i\pi_0)+i\lambda(\partial_sA_i)\varphi+i\lambda A_i\partial_s\varphi=(-i\lambda A_i\pi_0-i\lambda F_{0i}\varphi)+i\lambda F_{0i}\varphi+i\lambda A_i\pi_0=0$. Thus $C_i=0$ on the initial slice implies $C_i=0$ throughout the local time region, and the definition of $\pi_i$ in [L1] gives $\pi_i=D_i\varphi$. [given, L1, L2, A1, algebra]

2.1 The full closedness now proved gives $\partial_sF_{ij}-\partial_iF_{0j}+\partial_jF_{0i}=0$ in coordinates. Since $\partial_sA_i=F_{0i}$, differentiating $B_{ij}=F_{ij}-(\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i)$ gives $\partial_sB_{ij}=0$. Its initial value is zero, so $B_{ij}=0$; also $A_0=0$ gives $F_{0i}=\partial_sA_i-\partial_iA_0$. Consequently every component satisfies $F=dA$. Step 1.1 gives $\pi_i=D_i\varphi$, and $\partial_s\varphi=\pi_0$ with $A_0=0$ gives $\pi_0=D_0\varphi$, so $\pi=D\varphi$ in all slots. The reduced scalar divergence equation is therefore the actual scalar equation $E_\varphi=0$ in [L3]. [given, L1, L2, L3, step 1.1, step 1.3, algebra]

Thus, writing $e_i=h(e,\mathfrak e_i)$ and $b_i=h(b,\mathfrak e_i)$, its frame components are $F_\Sigma(\mathfrak e_i,n)=e_i$ and $F_\Sigma(\mathfrak e_i,\mathfrak e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$, with $\epsilon_{123}=+1$. Require $F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$, $\pi_i=(D_i\varphi_0)=\partial_i\varphi_0-i\lambda A_{\Sigma,i}\varphi_0$, and $A(n)=0$. Fix a smooth positive reference metric $\gamma$ and the product comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\gamma$ near the initial slice. The harmonic-gauge vector is $H^a:=g^{bc}(\Gamma(g)^a{}_{bc}-\Gamma(\bar g)^a{}_{bc})$; use the initial jet from [[lem-emg-fixed-smooth-background-harmonic-data]]:

Let $D$ be the Levi–Civita derivative of $h$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK$, and $T=T^{\mathrm{EM}}+T^\varphi$ be evaluated on the complete initial data. Define $j^0:=-n_aj^a$ in the normal frame and assume the sourced Maxwell and total-stress Einstein constraints

More generally, let $\Sigma$ be any smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary. Prescribe smooth $h$ positive definite, symmetric $K$, spatial vector fields $e,b$, a global one-form $A_\Sigma$, a complex scalar $\varphi_0$, and its independent normal derivative $\pi_n$. Define $F_\Sigma$ by the same $h,e,b$ convention in local positively oriented orthonormal frames, without requiring a global frame. Require $F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$, $\pi_i=D_i\varphi_0$, $A(n)=0$, and the sourced Maxwell and total-stress Einstein constraints displayed above at every point of $\Sigma$. Restrict to neighborhoods where $|\varphi|^2\in\mathcal U$. Then the data have a smooth local development near each initial point. Any two developments of this same fixed model and complete data are related near the initial surface by a data-fixing, time-orientation-preserving isometry and a global-potential gauge transformation

1.1 The prescribed normal/tangential two-form components determine the unique real two-form on $\mathbb R n\oplus T\Sigma$: $F(n,\mathfrak e_i)=-e_i$ and $F(\mathfrak e_i,\mathfrak e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$. Exactness $F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$ and $\pi_i=D_i\varphi_0$, together with $\pi_0=\pi_n$ in the initial temporal gauge, make all field and potential entries compatible. The jet in [L4] makes the harmonic vector initially zero. After the fixed invertible rescalings, every component is real and belongs to the stipulated $H^s$ class; the compact range lies in $K_0\Subset K_1\Subset O$. [given, F1, L1, L4, A1, construct]

5.1 Since $q_i=\partial_i g$ up to the fixed smooth background connection, the periodic Fourier norm identity gives $\|g\|_{H^{s+1}}\asymp\|g\|_{H^s}+\sum_i\|\partial_i g\|_{H^s}$; similarly $p=\bar\nabla_0g$ gives the stated time-derivative regularity. From $\pi_i=D_i\varphi$, one has $\partial_i\varphi=\pi_i+i\lambda A_i\varphi$. The $H^s$ algebra estimate in [L9] makes $A_i\varphi\in L^\infty H^s$, and the same estimate in $C H^{s-1}$ gives continuity of the spatial derivatives. The Fourier norm identity $\|f\|_{H^{r+1}}\asymp\|f\|_{H^r}+\sum_i\|\partial_i f\|_{H^r}$ then gives $\varphi\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$. The field-strength, potential, and $\pi$ regularities are the corresponding components of the reduced state. The embedding in [L9] supplies the classical derivatives needed by the equations at $s\ge5$. [given, L7, L9, step 2.1, step 4.1, algebra]

5.2 For general smooth $\Sigma$, regard $\Psi=(A,\operatorname{Re}\varphi,\operatorname{Im}\varphi)$ as the fixed covariant matter fields; $F=dA$, $\pi=D\varphi$, $j$, and $T$ are the fixed equations and tensorial expressions of [F1]. Thus the complete data and all initial auxiliary constraints are specified; $A(n)=0$ fixes the initial temporal gauge. The equations and stress are covariant under local diffeomorphisms because $d$, the metric connection, contractions, and the oriented volume form commute with pullback.
